title: Emergent quantum chaos from correlations on a random graph
authors: Mrinal Sarkar, Valerio Pagni, Tilman Enss, Nicolò Defenu
abstract: This work demonstrates that sparse long-range random bonds on a one-dimensional lattice alone can generate quantum-chaotic spectral correlations and also drive a localization transition in a noninteracting single-particle Hamiltonian. The model is a one-dimensional ring in which each pair of sites is connected independently with a probability $p_{ij}= d_{ij}^{-(1+σ)}$. Each bond carries identical unit hopping and on-site disorder is absent. Despite the absence of on-site disorder and interaction, the model displays quantum chaotic spectra with Gaussian orthogonal ensemble (GOE) level statistics at small $σ$ and localized eigenstates with Poisson statistics at larger $σ$. The transition occurs in the range $ 0.80 \lesssim σ_c \lesssim 0.85$, far above the summability threshold of the mean hopping profile ($σ=0$). A Gaussian field theory retaining only the mean and variance of the Bernoulli bonds instead predicts a threshold at $σ=1$, suggesting that higher cumulants are infrared-relevant. Our findings hint towards a universality class that is distinct from both the power-law random banded matrix model and the standard Anderson transition.
summary: The paper studies quantum chaotic behavior in 1D lattices with sparse, long-range random bonds. It numerically demonstrates an ergodic-to-localized transition at a critical bond disorder strength $\sigma_c$. Theoretically, it develops and analyzes a nonlinear sigma model, showing that capturing the full non-Gaussian nature of the disorder is crucial for accurately predicting this transition.
main_problem: The work investigates quantum chaos and localization transitions driven purely by geometric disorder (connectivity) rather than additive potential disorder.
main_result: A transition from ergodic/chaotic spectral correlations (GOE statistics) to localized states (Poisson statistics) is found at a critical exponent $\sigma_c$ significantly higher than naive theoretical predictions, suggesting the importance of higher-order correlation functions.
method: The analysis combines numerical diagonalization and spectral statistics with advanced field theory techniques, specifically deriving and analyzing a nonlinear sigma model for the disorder-averaged Green's function.
model_or_system: The system is a one-dimensional ring lattice where hopping bonds are added independently based on a probability $p_{ij} \propto d^{-(1+\sigma)}$, creating a sparse random graph structure. The Hamiltonian is non-interacting and purely geometric in its disorder.
key_observables: Nearest-neighbor level spacing distribution $P(s)$, consecutive-gap ratio $\langle r angle$, fractal dimension scaling $D_q$, and the effective action coefficient $\Pi(0) - \Pi(q)$.
important_parameters: The disorder exponent $\sigma$ controls connectivity; the transition occurs in the range $0.80 \lesssim \sigma_c \lesssim 0.85$.
main_assumptions: Field theory derivations rely on approximations like small-momentum expansions and retaining only up to second cumulants, which are shown to be insufficient for determining the true critical point.
figures_summary: Figures compare level spacing distributions ($P(s)$) showing crossover from GOE ($\sigma=0.5$) to Poisson ($\sigma=0.9$), and show fractal dimension scaling $D_q$ confirming ergodic vs. localized regimes.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from numerical evidence of the transition using spectral statistics, to developing a field-theoretic description via the nonlinear sigma model, culminating in deriving the leading nonanalytic contribution $\Pi(0) - \Pi(q)$ based on scaling arguments.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed theoretical framework for understanding how structural disorder alone can induce quantum chaos and localization, offering insights into universality classes distinct from standard Anderson models relevant to disordered quantum materials.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Hopping matrices for a typical disorder realization of the 1DLR3 graph with L = 16 sites and σ = 0.6. (a) Bernoulli disorder: Each off-diagonal element tij is 1 (Blue) with probability pij = d−(1+σ) ij and 0 (White) otherwise, yield- ing a sparse binary matrix. (b) Gaussian truncation: The matrix elements tij are replaced by a Gaussian with the same mean pij and variance pij(1 −pij), truncating at the second cumulant of the Bernoulli distribution. The resulting hopping matrix is dense and continuously distributed.

FIG. 2. Eigenvalue statistics for σ = 0.5 [panels(a), (c), (d)] and σ = 0.9 [panels (b), (c) and (d)]. Panels (a) and (b) show the level-spacing distribution P(s) for L = 220. FIG. 4. Mean gap ratio ⟨r⟩as a function of σ for L = 215 to 220. The curves cross over from the GOE value ⟨r⟩GOE ≈ 0.5307 at small σ to the Poisson value ⟨r⟩P ≈0.3863 at large σ, indicating an ergodic-to-localization transition be- tween σ = 0.80 and 0.85.

FIG. 3. Scaling of the fractal dimensions Dq for q = 2, 3, 4, 5 with inverse system size 1/L. Solid lines show results for σ = 0.5, where Dq tends to approach unity as L →∞, con- sistent with the GOE-like level statistics observed in Fig. 2, yielding an existence of ergodic phase. Dashed lines show re- sults for σ = 0.9, where Dq extrapolates to zero in the thermo- dynamic limit, confirming localization consistently with the level statistics.
